subject: Renewal: hybrid tranche + top-up window + term split playbook
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal proposal: hybrid tranche + top-up window + term split playbook

Hi Sarah —

Great chatting last week. Per our call I’m sending a concise proposal for Acme’s renewal that balances predictability for you with the flex you asked for around burst capacity. High level:

- Term: 24 months but split into a 12/12 tranche (year 1: committed baseline + reserved burst band; year 2: increased baseline with optional auto-top-up window)
- Ramp: month-over-month ramp in Q1 to avoid first-quarter spike charges; guaranteed minimum throughput in months 1–3
- Top-up window: a 45-day rolling top-up option each quarter for transient bursts (carry-forward of unused burst credits up to one quarter)
- Auto-renew: opt-in default with explicit opt-out 60 days prior to renewal; legacy SKUs will phase out at the start of year 2 to migrate to the new usage-first SKU
- Pricing: blended effective $/token across committed + burst bands; we’ll provide pro-rata credits for mid-term increases

Attachments: capacity_projection_Q4.xlsx (projected monthly burst profile), Acme_MAAP_v2_redlines.pdf (redlines on SOW/MAAP).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the tranche split (12/12) and whether Acme wants the 45-day top-up window enabled.
2) If yes, I’ll issue a redline-ready amendment and a mutual action plan (MAP) link for Procurement.
3) Once procurement signs, we’ll schedule a canary capacity add (2 weeks) to validate the burst path.

If you want, we can add a clause for symmetric true-up at month 12 with an optional early uplift credit.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

---

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: 2026-11-03T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: hybrid tranche + top-up window + term split playbook

Camila —

Thanks for the detailed note. A few clarifying Qs from Procurement and our infra team:

1) On the 45-day top-up window: can unused burst credits be carried forward only once (one quarter) or indefinitely? We want to avoid large year-end carry liabilities.
2) For the split-term: what happens if Acme accelerates usage in month 6 — do we get immediate access to year-2 baseline or is that handled via pro-rata top-up?
3) Canary capacity: who bears the canary validation cost? We expect Redwood to run the canary at no extra charge if it validates the model path.

Also Procurement asked for an initial redline by Nov 10; will you be able to get that over?

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme AI
On behalf of: James Li, Head of Infrastructure

---

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: hybrid tranche + top-up window + term split playbook

Sarah —

Great questions. Short answers:
1) Carry-forward: we propose carry-forward up to one quarter only (aligns with your ask to limit liabilities). That is the default in the attached redline; we can add a clause for unilateral reset at the end of each fiscal quarter if Acme prefers.
2) Early acceleration: accelerated usage in month 6 would be handled via a pro-rata top-up to the year-2 baseline. We can include an optional step-up discount schedule if you expect steady acceleration (helps reduce friction).
3) Canary: Redwood will run the canary validation pro-bono for this renewal (we’ll size it to simulate expected peak intervals).

I’ll get the initial redline to Procurement by Nov 9 EOD — attaching the redline draft now (Acme_MAAP_v2_redlines.pdf).

Action items for internal follow-up (cc’d Lauren + Marissa):
- Lauren: confirm whether the step-up discount ladder is feasible for this account (3 tiers: +25%, +50%, +100% baseline increases).
- Marissa: review the proposed pro-rata credit language for early uplift and the 45-day rolling top-up wording; want to ensure no unexpected SLO credit exposure.

Sarah, I’m happy to schedule a 20-min call with Procurement/Infra next week to walk the workbook.

Thanks,
Camila

---

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal: Acme — pricing ask and MAP timeline (internal)

Team — forwarding Acme thread. Quick summary + asks:

Summary: Acme is open to 24m split (12/12) with a 45-day quarterly top-up. Procurement wants redlines by Nov 10. Infra asked about early acceleration handling and canary validation costs.

Asks:
- Karthik: can we approve the step-up ladder (25/50/100) at the stated blended $/token levels? Recommend we keep year-1 floor conservative and use step-up discounts to incentivize quicker ramp.
- Marissa: please confirm pro-rata credit language — specifically, ensure we don’t create automatic long-term SLO credit liabilities for temporary health/perf incidents tied to burst behavior.
- Lauren: update MAP in HubSpot with proposed milestone dates (send redline, procurement sign, canary window, go-live).

I’ve attached the capacity workbook; please review ASAFP — Procurement expects a redline tomorrow.

Thanks —
Camila

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T14:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal: Acme — pricing ask and MAP timeline (internal)

Camila / team —

I reviewed the workbook and language. Approved with edits:

1) Step-up ladder: approved at 20%/40%/80% (instead of 25/50/100) to protect inventory; communicate as a negotiation buffer.
2) Pro-rata uplift: include a one-time true-up at month 12 with optional prepay credit applied to year 2; no ongoing SLO credits for burst-induced transient degradation — we’ll keep SLO credit triggers tied to sustained infra failure metrics.
3) Carry-forward: cap at one quarter and add a reset on fiscal year boundary; include a hard cap on carried credits equal to 10% of committed annual baseline.
4) Canary: Redwood runs validation pro-bono; we own any incremental infra costs for the canary if we choose non-standard hardware.

Camila — proceed to send the Nov 9 redline to Procurement with our edits and update the MAP. Lauren — please reflect the new milestone dates and the step-up ladder in HubSpot. Marissa — please sign off on the final SOW redline before I authorize counter-signature.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
